inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E = 9M-2026 actual net sales 13,504 (Q3-2026 10-Q) + Q4-2026 guidance midpoint ~5,250. Used as FY0 because the Q3-2026 balance sheet already contains nine months of FY2026 cash flow; Y1 = FY2027. The omitted Q4-2026 flow (~0.2bn after capex) is a small conservative bias.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: Q3-2026 weighted-average diluted shares 871m (863m basic + 8m dilutive awards; 15m anti-dilutive excluded), Q3-2026 10-Q Note 13. Cover count 861.4m basic at 2026-10-23. Held FLAT because SBC (incl. net-share-settlement taxes) is fully expensed in the flows. The $2.0bn ATM equity distribution agreement (Sep-2026) had sold no shares at Q3-2026; if drawn at ~$106 it would add ~19m shares (~2%) of genuine non-SBC issuance and should then be modelled explicitly.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to Q3-2026 from the cash-flow statements: share-based compensation expense 286 (FY2025 10-K) + 298 (9M-2026) - 216 (9M-2025) = 368; taxes paid on net-share settlement 98 + 294 - 87 = 305 (CSV equity_award_taxes). Corning publishes no combined SBC-plus-tax figure, so the two lines are summed. The 2026 tax line is inflated by the share price run-up between grant and vest (vest-date value, not grant-date expense); the forward sbc_pct path anchors at ~3.0% rather than the TTM 3.8%.
inputs.fcf_bridge_note: last_fcf = reported_fcf (TTM OCF 4,192 - TTM capex 1,731 = 2,461, company definition) - 1,000 upfront customer deposit received in 9M-2026 under a long-term supply agreement (Q3-2026 10-Q MD&A; non-recurring, it prepays future deliveries that the projection already books as revenue) - 673 SBC incl. equity-award taxes - 0 interest income = 788. Interest income (38 TTM) is NOT stripped because Corning is a net-debt company (net debt 5.7bn vs 0.8bn owner FCF); the cash is not added to EV twice. FY2025 audited owner FCF for reference: 1,413 - 286 - 98 = 1,029.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases 163m; 9M-2026 not material. Dividends ~1.0bn/yr. The flat count is a modelling convention the company is only partly funding via repurchases (the net-share-settlement tax payments are the main mechanism).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.2% (10-yr UST), beta ~1.15 (cyclical materials/optical), ERP 5.0% -> cost of equity ~10.0%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.6% (blended debentures 3.9-7.25%, finance leases 5.86%, yen/euro notes), ~3.7% after tax. Weights ~92% equity (market cap ~92bn) / 8% debt -> WACC ~9.5%. Held identical across scenarios: cyclicality, AI-capex and customer-concentration risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not a second time in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Mixed by lease class, each charged exactly once. (1) Finance leases (Hemlock solar equipment, 1,232 at FY2025 within 'Total long-term debt', ~1,150 at Q3-2026) are inside total_debt 8,200 -> treatment (A): principal payments (346 FY2025, 106 9M-2026, in financing) are NOT deducted from flows; renewal of leased assets is carried through the capex % path. (2) Operating leases (liabilities 943 at FY2025) are expensed inside operating income under ASC 842 -> treatment (B): cost already in EBITDA, liabilities EXCLUDED from net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest (Hemlock Semiconductor minority) deducted once in the equity bridge at Q3-2026 book value 617. Flows are consolidated; the Solar segment is near break-even (FY2025 -26m, 9M-2026 -7m), so the NCI share of forward flows is immaterial and book value is an adequate deduction.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: operating company, cyclical industrial/materials -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). First valuation of this ticker; no MEMORY entry. EBITDA basis is GAAP operating income + D&A + SBC at SPOT yen: the 'translated earnings contract' hedge gains (212 in 9M-2026) sit below operating income in GAAP and are excluded from the flows; the hedge book's net fair value is added in the equity bridge instead (matching-asset rule). Corning's 'core' results restate at hedged yen rates and are therefore not the DCF base. TTM adj. EBITDA margin 27.0% (OI 2,920 + D&A 1,492 + SBC 368 on 17,719); Q3-2026 run-rate ~27.6%. Working capital: receivables 3,101 + inventories 3,646 - payables 2,492 = 4,255 = 24% of TTM revenue, so growth consumes cash (capture negative); customer deposits under long-term agreements partially offset, hence -12% base rather than -24%. Cash tax: FY2025 taxes paid 283 on ~2,050 pre-tax = 13.8% (OBBBA full expensing; foreign mix); ramped to 20% (Corning's normal core rate) by Y5. Price: regular close; not an after-hours print. Note the stock has fallen ~61% from its 52-week high -- the price sits far below the high but the DCF still finds it above weighted owner-FCF value.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base scenario driver path, FY2026E->FY2031E CAGR (Springboard high-confidence case discounted for AI-capex cyclicality); historical equity CAGR is not a usable anchor for Corning
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (~0% 3-yr, -1.8% 5-yr) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (3.3%/6.7%) and EPS (6.2%/28.2%). Book equity is held down by ~1.0bn/yr dividends, repurchases and yen translation losses, so it does not track the business; growth anchored to the forward driver path instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (OCF - capex - SBC - equity-award taxes, USD m): FY2021 1,524; FY2022 789; FY2023 291; FY2024 620; FY2025 1,029; TTM Q3-2026 788 ex the 1.0bn one-off deposit (1,788 including it). fcf_3yr is FY2022->FY2025 on owner FCF (9.3%) vs 11.8% on reported FCF: SBC plus net-share-settlement taxes grew faster than cash flow. fcf_5yr is actually the 4-yr FY2021->FY2025 CAGR (FY2020 capex is not in the extracted filings); it is negative because FY2021 was a display-cycle peak. EPS 5-yr CAGR is off a depressed FY2020 base (0.54). The history shows the cyclicality the bear case encodes: revenue fell 11% in FY2023 and owner FCF fell 81% peak-to-trough FY2021->FY2023.

base.growth_note: FY2030 revenue ~28.9bn (10.7% CAGR from FY2026E) vs management's high-confidence end-2030 run-rate of 35bn (~33bn full-year) and internal 40bn. Discounts the Springboard plan for AI data-centre capex cyclicality and a flat display/auto/life-sciences portfolio; it is still ~3x Corning's 2017-2024 revenue CAGR.
base.margin_note: Adj. EBITDA (pre-SBC, spot yen) 27.5% Y1 vs 27.0% TTM / ~27.6% Q3-2026 run-rate; peaks 28.5% on Optical mix then eases to 28% as the mix matures and display pricing normalises.
base.capex_note: FY2026 guided 2.0bn (10.7% of revenue) for Hickory NC fiber and Solar; 2021-2026 range 7.4-11.6%. Terminal 8.0% vs D&A 7.8% is consistent with 2.5% growth for a capital-intensive manufacturer.

bull.growth_note: Tracks management's HIGH-CONFIDENCE Springboard case, not the internal plan: FY2030 revenue ~33bn (~35bn exit run-rate). The internal 40bn case is deliberately not modelled.

bear.growth_note: AI capex digestion in 2028-29 coincides with a display-glass pricing cycle: revenue flat then -4%, mirroring FY2023 (-11%). Trough EBITDA margin 20% matches the FY2023 level (GAAP OI 7.1% + D&A 10.9% + SBC 1.7%). Capex is cut to 7% as expansion pauses; D&A rises as a share of lower revenue.

scenario_narratives.base: The AI data-centre fiber build-out carries Optical Communications (44% of sales, growing ~40%) for two more years, then decelerates as hyperscaler capex normalises; Glass Innovations, Automotive and Life Sciences stay roughly flat in aggregate and Solar ramps to modest profitability on 45X credits. Revenue reaches ~29bn by FY2030 -- well short of the 35-40bn Springboard run-rate targets -- while adj. EBITDA margin rises ~1pp on Optical mix before easing. Capex stays at 9-10% of sales through 2029 (Hickory, Solar), working capital absorbs ~12% of each revenue dollar added, and cash tax ramps from ~16% to Corning's normal ~20%. Owner FCF margin climbs from ~9% to ~14% as capex intensity normalises; the business is valued as a capital-intensive materials manufacturer with a strong but cyclical demand window, not as a software-like compounder.
scenario_narratives.bull: Management's high-confidence Springboard case plays out: multi-year hyperscaler contracts (Meta up to 6bn through 2030, plus Nvidia/OpenAI/Google/Amazon/Microsoft demand) sustain ~20%/18%/14% growth through 2029, revenue reaches ~33bn in FY2030, and the Optical mix shift lifts adj. EBITDA margin to ~31%. Customer deposits and government incentives fund a larger share of capacity, so capex intensity falls to 7.5% after 2030 and working-capital drag is lighter. Display pricing stays rational against AGC/NEG and Solar becomes a genuine third leg. The 15x terminal cap binds, so the bull value does not depend on a software multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: A hyperscaler digestion period arrives in 2028 -- orders pause, an optical architecture shift or inventory correction hits fiber and connectivity pricing -- while display glass enters another pricing down-cycle and Asian competitors take share. Revenue is flat in FY2028 and falls 4% in FY2029 (FY2023 fell 11%), adj. EBITDA margin troughs at 20% (the FY2023 level), and customer concentration (Meta, panel makers) turns from asset to liability. Management cuts capex to 7% of sales and tax falls with profits; recovery is to a permanently lower 2.5-3% growth path at a 23% margin. Working capital releases cash in the down years but the bear value still sits at a fraction of the current price, which is the measure of how much AI-cycle continuation the market is paying for.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: roughly half of recent growth and most of the incremental profit come from one end-market (AI data-centre capex) with a handful of hyperscaler customers, and Corning's own history (FY2017 and FY2023 revenue declines, owner FCF -81% peak-to-trough 2021-23) shows how hard its cycles bite. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it requires hyperscaler capex to run at pace through 2030 AND display pricing to hold AND Solar to execute -- three independent things -- even though it only tracks management's high-confidence (not internal) case and management has beaten every Springboard target so far. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Corning is valued as what it is: a capital-intensive specialty-materials manufacturer in an unusually strong demand window. The flows are owner FCF -- GAAP operating income at spot yen, SBC plus net-share-settlement taxes expensed, the one-off 1.0bn customer deposit stripped, growth-driven working capital charged, capex held near D&A only once the build-out is done -- discounted at a single 9.5% USD WACC with cyclicality carried in the scenario flows and weights. The terminal multiple is capped at 15x FCF (cyclical rule). Management's Springboard targets are treated as the bull case ceiling, not the base.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI data-centre capex cycle: Optical Communications is ~44% of sales and the majority of incremental profit; a hyperscaler pause or architecture shift is the single largest swing factor (bear case)
Customer concentration: Meta contract up to 6bn through 2030; a few panel makers dominate Glass Innovations
Display glass pricing cycles and Asian competition (AGC, NEG) -- the source of the FY2017 and FY2023 downturns
Capex intensity: FY2026 capex 2.0bn vs D&A ~1.5bn; the model assumes intensity normalises to 8% of sales after 2030 -- if Corning must keep building, owner FCF stays depressed
Yen exposure: GAAP flows are at spot (~150/USD); the hedge book (net +464m) is finite and added in the bridge, not perpetuated in the margin
Solar/Hemlock dependence on 45X/48C/48D incentives and execution of the wafer/module ramp (NCI 617m deducted at book)
Potential ATM equity issuance (2.0bn authorised, none sold) would add ~2% genuine dilution not in the flat share count
Tax: IRS 2015-2020 examinations and South Korea disputes; cash tax ramped to 20% but a settlement would be a one-off outflow
